newsitem.title: USA: Circuit Systems says if sales slow, could hurt Q1.
newsitem.headline: Circuit Systems says if sales slow, could hurt Q1.

text.p: Circuit Systems Inc, which makes printed circuit boards, said Monday it expects its fiscal 1998 first quarter results could be severely hurt if sluggish sales continue.
"Although it is not clear how long the slowdown will last, the results of operations for the first quarter of fiscal year 1998 will be severely impacted," said President D.S. Patel in a news release.
The company added, however, that it has recently expanded capacity and has aggressive plans to seek new customers.
Earlier today, Circuit Systems reported sales for its fiscal year ended April 30, 1997 declined 2.6 percent from the same period a year ago to $63.4 million.

Fiscal year earnings fell to $0.40 a share from $0.58 a year ago due to the sales decline and higher expenses from a physical reorganization of plants, increase in capacity and costs associated with talks earlier in the year to merge with DDL Electronics Inc. The talks were abandoned.

Patel also said it has successfully concluded its due diligence in connection with a proposed purchase of the printed circuit board plant of Philips Consumer Electronics Co, a division of Philips North America Corp, and has targeted July 25, 1997 as the closing date for the purchase.

The company previously said that the purchase of this plant located in Greeneville, Tenn., is estimated to add $20 million to $25 million in annual sales and will help the company reach its goal of $100 million in sales in fiscal 1999.
Shares of Circuit Systems were trading up 6/16 to 4-15/16.
